1	# Plan for #230: a web control surface on the remote port
2	
3	Worktree `/Users/sbgragent/.dispatch/worktrees/f96f6569` at 0.4.1; every
4	line number is from this tree. One commit; the app runs at every step.
5	Facts are cited as `facts: Settled`, `facts: Unresolved` or `facts: For
6	the owner`.
7	
8	## Where this departs from the issue
9	
10	- **The session list carries no excerpt.** The issue's list shows "the
11	  one-line excerpt the card shows". No wire view carries one yet:
12	  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has `card`, `waiting`
13	  and `waiting_reason` and no excerpt field, and adding one is a wire
14	  crate change plus masking on the frame (`docs/remote-client.md:201`),
15	  outside this cut. The list shows kind, the card's word and the
16	  waiting reason; the session view shows the last response or the
17	  screen. The spec sentence at `docs/remote-client.md:207` is reworded
18	  in this commit to say the field is not yet on the wire; the field is
19	  a known gap in design.md.
20	- **The code rides in the URL's fragment, not its query.** The issue
21	  writes `/?code=…`. A fragment is never sent to the server (facts:
22	  Settled, RFC 3986 §3.5), so the code cannot reach a request log by
23	  any future change to `refuse`, which today logs path without query
24	  (`src/app.rs:3754-3766`). The page reads `location.hash` and clears
25	  it the same way the issue says; the camera-to-browser unknown is the
26	  same for both forms (facts: For the owner). The URL is
27	  `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
28	- **The browser's trust step is the certificate warning, and the page
29	  works without the WebSocket.** The issue offers click-through or a
30	  downloadable certificate. Downloading cannot work with the identity
31	  the spec fixed: iOS trusts no server certificate without a SAN, over
32	  825 days or without EKU (facts: Settled, Apple 103769), and lists a
33	  certificate for trust only when it is CA-shaped (facts: Settled, Apple
34	  DTS), so "download" means a CA plus a leaf, a different identity model
35	  from `docs/remote-client.md:307-308` (one self-signed certificate,
36	  SPKI pinned). That is a follow-up for the owner, not this plan. The
37	  click-through is the trust step, said in the dialog. Whether the
38	  bypass extends to `wss://` on iOS Safari is unresolved (facts:
39	  Unresolved, against it), so the page polls over `fetch` by default and
40	  the socket is the enhancement behind it.
41	- Everything else in the issue is as the tree bears it out.
42	
43	## The record
44	
45	No record changes. A browser is a `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:95-108`)
46	written by `Effect::SaveDevices` on `AppAction::Paired`
47	(`src/core/remote.rs:66-72`), its name from the page's user agent,
48	listed and revoked in the dialog as any device. No serialized type
49	changes, so no schema bump.
50	
51	The page's state on the device: the token is in an `HttpOnly` cookie
52	the host sets and script never reads; the page keeps only `server_id`
53	and `spki_sha256` from the pairing in `localStorage`, to say "identity
54	changed" later (both are public, `/info` serves them to anyone).
55	
56	## The signals
57	
58	No new signal.
59	
60	## The actions and effects
61	
62	No new `AppAction` or `Effect`. The changes are in the adapter, the
63	frame's request routing, and one pure function in the core.
64	
65	### Decision 1: browser trust (the click-through)
66	
67	The warning the owner clicks through on the local network is the trust
68	step. What the `key` in the URL buys: a genuine page refuses to post the
69	code to a host whose `/info` key differs, which is the native client's
70	check; what it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not a
71	genuine page, so the owner's eyes on the warning, on their own network,
72	stand in for the SPKI pin. The paired-devices dialog says so in one
73	sentence (UI below). The host side is unchanged: no non-loopback bind
74	serves anything but `/info`, `/pair` and now the three page files before
75	pairing (§5, `docs/remote-client.md:306` amended). Chrome remembers the
76	bypass for a week per host (facts: Settled); Safari's persistence is
77	unknown (facts: Unresolved), so the dialog's sentence says the warning
78	may return and the page loses nothing when it does (the cookie and the
79	stored ids survive a reload).
80	
81	### Decision 2: the token reaches the WebSocket as a cookie
82	
83	The cookie is the safer store (script cannot read an `HttpOnly` cookie;
84	anything in `localStorage` or a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value is in
85	script), and the settled facts say it reaches both `fetch` and the
86	WebSocket on an IP origin with `Secure; SameSite=Strict` and no `Domain`
87	(facts: Settled, RFC 6265bis and HTML "obtain a site"). Whether a browser
88	stores a `Secure` cookie on a bypassed-certificate origin is unresolved
89	(facts: Unresolved): **that is the first thing the implementer tests on
90	a phone, before anything else is built**, with the host's `/pair`
91	answering a cookie and a `curl`-free check that `/api/v1/waiting` then
92	answers 200 from the page. If it fails, the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`
93	transport is a follow-up (end of plan), not a second transport built
94	now. The page shows "pair again" when its first authenticated call after
95	`/pair` is refused, so a dropped cookie is a visible state, never a
96	silent one.
97	
98	Mechanics:
99	
100	- `POST /api/v1/pair` takes an additive body field `"transport":
101	  "cookie"`. With it, the reply body omits `token` and carries
102	  `Set-Cookie: switchboard_token=<token>; Path=/api/v1/; Secure;
103	  HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`. Without it (the headset, the CLI,
104	  `tests/remote.rs::pair` at 406) the reply is as today, token in the
105	  body, no cookie. `remote_pair` (`src/app.rs:3606-3674`) is the only
106	  change on the frame; `Path=/api/v1/` keeps the cookie off the page
107	  files, which need none.
108	- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-517`) reads the `cookie`
109	  header, finds the `switchboard_token=` pair, and puts its value in a
110	  new `RemoteRequest::cookie: Option<String>` field. `authenticate`
111	  (`src/app.rs:3127-3157`) takes `bearer` first and `cookie` second:
112	  the native clients are unchanged, and a browser never sets the
113	  bearer. The WebSocket upgrade authenticates on the same request, so
114	  the socket needs nothing new; `respond_upgrade`
115	  (`remote.rs:519-527`) is unchanged.
116	- A 401 for an unknown cookie token (revoked, or every token after a key
117	  rotation) carries `Set-Cookie: switchboard_token=; Path=/api/v1/;
118	  Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, so the browser drops
119	  it. The refusal text stays "the token is not known; pair again":
120	  "revoked" and "never paired" remain one answer on the wire (facts:
121	  Settled), and the page tells them apart itself (UI below).
122	- `SameSite=Strict` is the cross-site guard: a page on another origin
123	  cannot make the browser attach the cookie to a `fetch` or a WebSocket
124	  handshake to the host. No `Origin` check is added.
125	- The spec's "never in a URL" rule stands (`docs/remote-client.md:312`);
126	  the sentence gains "or as the cookie `/pair` sets for a browser".
127	
128	### Decision 3: one invite, the URL
129	
130	The QR and "Copy invite" carry the URL. A new pure function in
131	`src/core/remote.rs`, `pairing_invite(identity: &Identity, address:
132	&str, code: &str) -> String`, builds it (IPv6 bracketed, code uppercase,
133	`key` the full hex `spki_sha256` so the page compares it with `/info`
134	by string equality), shared by the dialog, `tests/remote.rs` and
135	`src/core/tests.rs`. The URL is 153 bytes, QR version 9 at 53 modules,
136	smaller than today's JSON at version 10 (facts: Settled); `QR_SCALE`
137	(`src/ui/remote.rs:42`) stays 4, and rises only if the owner finds it
138	unreadable (facts: For the owner). The JSON form is no longer produced
139	by the host; the native text path keeps parsing it so an old copied
140	invite still works:
141	
142	- `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114-116`)
143	  branches: text starting with `https://` has its authority taken as
144	  text, the substring between `https://` and the first `/`, straight
145	  into `addresses: [that]`, so the brackets the host wrote around an
146	  IPv6 literal survive; the fragment after `#` is split on `&` into
147	  `code`, `key`, `id`. Anything else is the JSON as today. `parse` uses
148	  nothing from `SwitchboardTransport`. `switchboard-remote pair
149	  '<url>'` (`main.swift:107-125`), the headset's paste field
150	  (`BrowserView.swift:883`) and `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` per line
151	  (`BrowserView.swift:104-108`) all pass through `parse` and need no
152	  other change; the three-argument CLI path (`main.swift:112-118`) is
153	  unchanged.
154	
155	Without a network address (`remote::local_address()` is `None`,
156	`remote.rs:962-973`) there is no URL: the dialog shows the code and the
157	key with no QR and no Copy invite, and the sentence says to pair by the
158	CLI's three-argument form. The address is the default route's source
159	(facts: Settled); a VPN taking the default route makes it unreachable
160	from the phone (facts: For the owner), and listing every interface is a
161	follow-up.
162	
163	### Decision 4: static paths on the allowlisted port
164	
165	The served set, all `GET`, all before authentication, matched exactly
166	in `serve_remote` (`src/app.rs:3017-3024`) ahead of the `/api/v1/`
167	prefix so the allowlist stays in one place:
168	
169	| Path | Content-Type | Body |
170	|---|---|---|
171	| `/` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` | `web/index.html` |
172	| `/app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.css` |
173	| `/app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.js` |
174	
175	Every other path, `/index.html` and `/app.js/` included, and every
176	other method on these three, stays 404 `not_found` as today. Each
177	static reply carries:
178	
179	- `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
180	  style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none';
181	  form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src 'self'`
182	  covers the same-host `wss://` in CSP3 and WebKit since 2022
183	  (facts: Settled). No inline script, no inline style, no external
184	  resource: the HTML has one `<link>` and one `<script src>`.
185	- `Cache-Control: no-store`, so a new version is what the next open
186	  gets and nothing is cached across versions.
187	- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
188	
189	Pool and window: a page load is unauthenticated and sits in the
190	four-slot stranger pool (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `remote.rs:567`) until
191	its first authenticated reply. The count the page is designed to: three
192	load connections for the three files, kept alive; the first
193	authenticated request is a `fetch` of `/api/v1/waiting`, which moves its
194	connection to the paired pool and frees a slot; the WebSocket opens only
195	after that reply, as the fourth stranger at worst. Whether a browser
196	retries a dropped extra connection is unresolved (facts: Unresolved);
197	the poll fallback (page step 5) covers a socket that was dropped. The
198	three paths get
199	their own rate window, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 120` per listener (a reload
200	is three requests), beside `PAIR_PER_MINUTE` and `INFO_PER_MINUTE`
201	(`remote.rs:584-587`, `Limits::limited` at 631), answered 429 past it
202	without reaching the frame. §4.1's bounds list gains the line.
203	
204	`RemoteReply` (`remote.rs:389-393`) gains an additive field
205	`headers: Vec<(String, String)>`, written after `Content-Length` by
206	`respond` (`remote.rs:530-554`), which takes the reply rather than
207	`(status, body)`; `Content-Type` is a header in that list, defaulting
208	to `application/json` when absent, so the 28 literals in `src/app.rs`
209	and the two in the adapter change only by `headers: Vec::new()`.
210	`Set-Cookie` travels the same way. `Served::Now`
211	(`app.rs:277-280`) is how the static replies go out; bodies are
212	`include_str!` constants in a new `src/web.rs` (`pub const INDEX_HTML`,
213	`APP_CSS`, `APP_JS`), the pattern of `include_bytes!` for the icon and
214	fonts (`src/main.rs:167`, `src/ui/theme.rs:203-211`). Nothing in
215	`Cargo.toml` changes.
216	
217	### What the page does (`web/app.js`)
218	
219	In order, on load:
220	
221	1. Read `location.hash`; if it names `code`, `key` and `id`, call
222	   `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` before any request. The
223	   fragment never reaches the host (facts: Settled); a copy in the
224	   browser's history is a spent single-use code once pairing succeeds
225	   or the window closes (facts: Unresolved on `replaceState` and
226	   history; `docs/remote-client.md:311` on single use), and the plan
227	   says so in the spec's new paragraph rather than promising more.
228	2. `GET /api/v1/info`. If the stored `server_id` matches and
229	   `spki_sha256` differs: show "This host's identity changed. Pair
230	   again." and send nothing else. If the URL's `key` differs from
231	   `/info`'s: show "This is not the host whose code was scanned." and
232	   do not post the code.
233	3. With a code and a matching key: `POST /api/v1/pair` with
234	   `{code, spki_sha256, device_name, transport: "cookie"}`;
235	   `device_name` from `navigator.userAgent` as "Safari on iPhone",
236	   "Chrome on Android", "Safari on Mac"; an iPad presents as a Mac
237	   (facts: Settled), so `Macintosh` with `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1`
238	   is "Safari on iPad". Store `server_id` and `spki_sha256`. A 403
239	   `wrong_code` or `pairing_closed` is shown by its message.
240	4. `GET /api/v1/waiting`, the first authenticated request. A 401 here
241	   with no pairing ever stored shows "Not paired. Open Remote devices on the Mac and scan the code."; a 401
242	   with a stored pairing shows "This device was revoked. Pair again."
243	   (the cookie is already cleared by the host). Then step 5, then
244	   `/projects` and `/projects/{id}/sessions` per project.
245	5. Open `wss://<host>/api/v1/events` after the `/waiting` reply of
246	   step 4 and before the `projects` and `sessions` snapshots (so one
247	   connection is already in the paired pool, Decision 4), buffer
248	   events, apply by revision (§4.4 "Subscribe first, then snapshot":
249	   the collections are the snapshot, `/waiting` is refetched if an
250	   event's revision passes its own),
251	   send `watch {kind, id}` for the open session's `conversation` or
252	   `screen` key. On open failure or close: poll `waiting`, `projects`
253	   and the open session's content every 5 s, refetching a collection
254	   whose `revision` moved, and retry the socket every 30 s. Header says
255	   "live" or "polling".
256	6. Render: sessions grouped by project, waiting first within and across
257	   groups, each with kind, the card word, the waiting reason; tapping
258	   one opens the view: `GET sessions/{id}/last-response` for a Claude
259	   Code session (`text`, as `client/Fixtures/last_response.json`),
260	   `GET sessions/{id}/screen` for anything else (`text`), refreshed on
261	   `changed {conversation|screen}` or on the poll. A reply box posts
262	   `POST sessions/{id}/send {op, text}` with a fresh UUID `op`, shown
263	   only when `/pair`'s or the stored `scope` is `control`; the device's
264	   scope and the host's `server_name` are in the header. Scope is not
265	   on `/info`, so a scope lowered in the dialog reaches the page as the
266	   403 its next `send` answers, which it shows as "This device is
267	   read-only now."
268	
269	No framework, no build step: three files, plain DOM.
270	
271	## The UI
272	
273	`src/ui/remote.rs` `pairing` (141-228): the payload at 160-165 becomes
274	`core::remote::pairing_invite(..)`; the sentence becomes "Scan with a
275	phone's camera, or paste the invite into a client. The browser will
276	warn about the certificate: on your own network, accepting it is the
277	trust step, and it may ask again. Grants … scope. Open for five
278	minutes or three wrong codes." Without an address: no QR, no Copy
279	invite, "No network address: pair by `switchboard-remote pair
280	<host:port> <code> <key>`". `devices` (230-276) is unchanged: a browser
281	row reads "Safari on iPhone", read or control, paired and seen ago,
282	Revoke. No new script line: `pairing <code>` and `remote-devices`
283	(`src/script.rs:729-736`) already reach the window.
284	
285	## The tests
286	
287	Core (`src/core/tests.rs`): `pairing_invite` builds the URL with an
288	IPv4 and a bracketed IPv6 address, uppercases the code, carries the
289	full key and the id in the fragment, and never the token.
290	
291	`tests/remote.rs` (the `http` helper at 245-297 gains a `cookie`
292	argument and returns the response headers; `call` at 299 and `get`
293	follow; `subscribe_at` at 1960 gains a cookie variant):
294	
295	- `the_page_is_served_unpaired_with_its_headers`: `/`, `/app.css`,
296	  `/app.js` answer 200 with the content types, CSP, `no-store`,
297	  `nosniff`; `/index.html`, `/app.js/`, `/other` and `POST /` are 404
298	  `not_found`; the `/other` line in
299	  `info_is_served_to_anyone_and_every_other_read_is_refused_unpaired`
300	  (`tests/remote.rs:464`, the test at 426) stays.
301	- `the_page_references_only_what_the_host_serves`: every `src` and
302	  `href` in `web::INDEX_HTML` is one of the three paths; no `<script>`
303	  has a body; no `style=`, no `http://` or `https://` in any of the
304	  three files; `web::APP_JS` never contains `Authorization` (the token
305	  never enters script) and never writes `document.cookie`.
306	- `a_browser_pairs_from_the_invite_and_reads_through_its_cookie`: open
307	  the window, build the invite with `pairing_invite`, parse its
308	  fragment, `GET /info`, compare `key`, `POST /pair` with `transport:
309	  cookie` and `device_name: "Safari on iPhone"`; the body has no
310	  `token`, the `Set-Cookie` header has the name, `HttpOnly`, `Secure`,
311	  `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/api/v1/`; `GET /waiting` with the cookie is
312	  200 and `DeviceSeen` moved `last_seen`; the events upgrade with the
313	  cookie gets `hello`; the device is listed by name; a bearer in the
314	  same request outranks the cookie (a known bearer and an unknown
315	  cookie: 200). Then `RevokeDevice`: the next `GET` is 401 with a
316	  clearing `Set-Cookie` and the subscriber's socket closes (the pattern
317	  of the existing revocation test). The same test asserts the existing
318	  `pair` helper's native reply has the token in the body and no
319	  `Set-Cookie`.
320	- `a_page_load_fits_the_stranger_pool`: three connections each `GET`
321	  one page file and are held open (keep-alive, not closed); a fourth
322	  does `GET /waiting` with the cookie (200, moved to the paired pool)
323	  and a fifth then upgrades to the events socket with the cookie and
324	  receives `hello`, while the three are still held.
325	- `the_page_window_is_rate_limited`: the 121st static `GET` in a minute
326	  is 429, the shape of `pair_is_rate_limited_per_listener` (1406).
327	- Fixtures: `write_fixtures` (1587) adds `client/Fixtures/invite.txt`
328	  with the URL form; `the_client_fixtures_decode_on_both_sides` (1829)
329	  asserts the fixture equals `pairing_invite(..)` over the fixture
330	  identity, and the Swift side gains `testInviteParsesTheURL` reading
331	  that fixture beside the kept inline JSON test
332	  (`FixturesTests.swift:158-166`); the Swift test is the parser's test.
333	  No view fixture changes.
334	
335	`tests/ui.rs` `remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device`
336	(7424-7489): the clipboard assertion parses the URL: starts with
337	`https://`, the fragment carries `code=<code>` and the identity's full
338	`spki_sha256` as `key`.
339	
340	Not driven by a test, done by hand before the commit and recorded in
341	the PR: the cookie on a bypassed certificate (the Decision 2 check),
342	and the acceptance steps from the issue on one phone.
343	
344	## Docs, in the same commit
345	
346	- `docs/remote-client.md`: §4.1 bounds gain the page window; §4.3 table
347	  gains the three rows with scope "none" and the "everything else is
348	  refused" sentence names them; the `last_message` sentence at 207
349	  becomes "the excerpt is not yet on the wire; it will be a redacted
350	  field of the session view, masked as the redaction list above says",
351	  so 201 and 207 agree; §5 line 306 becomes "before
352	  anything but `/info`, `/pair` and the page", line 309 the URL, line
353	  312 the cookie clause, and a new paragraph "Browser trust" with
354	  Decision 1 and the fragment note; §13 Authentication row gains "a
355	  browser pairs from the invite URL and holds its token in an HttpOnly
356	  cookie".
357	- `docs/design.md` remote status (3107-3584): a bullet "**The web page
358	  (2026-10-22).**" after the typed-code bullet, and the known-gaps
359	  bullet gains the excerpt not on the wire, the socket-on-iOS and the
360	  one-address items.
361	- `README.md`: Layout rows 383, 401, 423, 437, 446 amended; new rows
362	  for `src/web.rs` and `web/`; the dev-aid paragraph at 267-279 says
363	  the invite is a URL a phone opens and that `switchboard-remote pair
364	  "$(pbpaste)"` still takes it.
365	- `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased: "The remote port serves a browser page:
366	  scan the pairing QR with a phone to see the sessions, the waiting
367	  ones first, read a session's last response or screen and reply."
368	
369	## Follow-ups for the owner (not in this commit)
370	
371	The excerpt on the wire, the socket on iOS and the one address are in
372	the design.md known-gaps bullet above. Beyond those:
373	
374	- Reissuing the leaf with an IP SAN and 825-day validity from the same
375	  key, or a CA-plus-leaf identity, so a device can trust the host
376	  instead of bypassing: a change to the identity model in §5.
377	- `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` as the token transport, only if the cookie
378	  fails the Decision 2 check on the owner's phone.
379	- Dispatch tickets and the full conversation on the page, as the issue
380	  defers.
381	
382	## Commit
383	
384	`Remote port serves a browser page paired from the invite URL`
385	
386	## Contract additions (copy into the commit message)
387	
388	- `RemoteRequest::cookie: Option<String>` (the `switchboard_token`
389	  cookie's value), `src/adapters/remote.rs`.
390	- `RemoteReply::headers: Vec<(String, String)>`, `src/adapters/remote.rs`.
391	- `core::remote::pairing_invite(&Identity, &str, &str) -> String`,
392	  `src/core/remote.rs`.
393	- `web::{INDEX_HTML, APP_CSS, APP_JS}`, new module `src/web.rs`
394	  embedding `web/index.html`, `web/app.css`, `web/app.js`.
395	- `POST /api/v1/pair` body field `transport: "cookie"`; `GET /`,
396	  `GET /app.css`, `GET /app.js` on the remote port.
397	- `PairingInvite.parse` accepts the URL form, `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift`.

### Decision 1: browser trust (the click-through)

The warning the owner clicks through on the local network is the trust
step. What the `key` in the URL buys: a genuine page refuses to post the
code to a host whose `/info` key differs, which is the native client's
check; what it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not a
genuine page, so the owner's eyes on the warning, on their own network,
stand in for the SPKI pin. The paired-devices dialog says so in one
sentence (UI below). The host side is unchanged: no non-loopback bind
serves anything but `/info`, `/pair` and now the three page files before
pairing (§5, `docs/remote-client.md:306` amended). Chrome remembers the
bypass for a week per host (facts: Settled); Safari's persistence is
unknown (facts: Unresolved), so the dialog's sentence says the warning
may return and the page loses nothing when it does (the cookie and the
stored ids survive a reload).

### Decision 2: the token reaches the WebSocket as a cookie

The cookie is the safer store (script cannot read an `HttpOnly` cookie;
anything in `localStorage` or a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value is in
script), and the settled facts say it reaches both `fetch` and the
WebSocket on an IP origin with `Secure; SameSite=Strict` and no `Domain`
(facts: Settled, RFC 6265bis and HTML "obtain a site"). Whether a browser
stores a `Secure` cookie on a bypassed-certificate origin is unresolved
(facts: Unresolved): **that is the first thing the implementer tests on
a phone, before anything else is built**, with the host's `/pair`
answering a cookie and a `curl`-free check that `/api/v1/waiting` then
answers 200 from the page. If it fails, the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`
transport is a follow-up (end of plan), not a second transport built
now. The page shows "pair again" when its first authenticated call after
`/pair` is refused, so a dropped cookie is a visible state, never a
silent one.

Mechanics:

- `POST /api/v1/pair` takes an additive body field `"transport":
  "cookie"`. With it, the reply body omits `token` and carries
  `Set-Cookie: switchboard_token=<token>; Path=/api/v1/; Secure;
  HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`. Without it (the headset, the CLI,
  `tests/remote.rs::pair` at 406) the reply is as today, token in the
  body, no cookie. `remote_pair` (`src/app.rs:3606-3674`) is the only
  change on the frame; `Path=/api/v1/` keeps the cookie off the page
  files, which need none.
- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-517`) reads the `cookie`
  header, finds the `switchboard_token=` pair, and puts its value in a
  new `RemoteRequest::cookie: Option<String>` field. `authenticate`
  (`src/app.rs:3127-3157`) takes `bearer` first and `cookie` second:
  the native clients are unchanged, and a browser never sets the
  bearer. The WebSocket upgrade authenticates on the same request, so
  the socket needs nothing new; `respond_upgrade`
  (`remote.rs:519-527`) is unchanged.
- A 401 for an unknown cookie token (revoked, or every token after a key
  rotation) carries `Set-Cookie: switchboard_token=; Path=/api/v1/;
  Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, so the browser drops
  it. The refusal text stays "the token is not known; pair again":
  "revoked" and "never paired" remain one answer on the wire (facts:
  Settled), and the page tells them apart itself (UI below).
- `SameSite=Strict` is the cross-site guard: a page on another origin
  cannot make the browser attach the cookie to a `fetch` or a WebSocket
  handshake to the host. No `Origin` check is added.
- The spec's "never in a URL" rule stands (`docs/remote-client.md:312`);
  the sentence gains "or as the cookie `/pair` sets for a browser".

### Decision 3: one invite, the URL

The QR and "Copy invite" carry the URL. A new pure function in
`src/core/remote.rs`, `pairing_invite(identity: &Identity, address:
&str, code: &str) -> String`, builds it (IPv6 bracketed, code uppercase,
`key` the full hex `spki_sha256` so the page compares it with `/info`
by string equality), shared by the dialog, `tests/remote.rs` and
`src/core/tests.rs`. The URL is 153 bytes, QR version 9 at 53 modules,
smaller than today's JSON at version 10 (facts: Settled); `QR_SCALE`
(`src/ui/remote.rs:42`) stays 4, and rises only if the owner finds it
unreadable (facts: For the owner). The JSON form is no longer produced
by the host; the native text path keeps parsing it so an old copied
invite still works:

- `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114-116`)
  branches: text starting with `https://` has its authority taken as
  text, the substring between `https://` and the first `/`, straight
  into `addresses: [that]`, so the brackets the host wrote around an
  IPv6 literal survive; the fragment after `#` is split on `&` into
  `code`, `key`, `id`. Anything else is the JSON as today. `parse` uses
  nothing from `SwitchboardTransport`. `switchboard-remote pair
  '<url>'` (`main.swift:107-125`), the headset's paste field
  (`BrowserView.swift:883`) and `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` per line
  (`BrowserView.swift:104-108`) all pass through `parse` and need no
  other change; the three-argument CLI path (`main.swift:112-118`) is
  unchanged.

Without a network address (`remote::local_address()` is `None`,
`remote.rs:962-973`) there is no URL: the dialog shows the code and the
key with no QR and no Copy invite, and the sentence says to pair by the
CLI's three-argument form. The address is the default route's source
(facts: Settled); a VPN taking the default route makes it unreachable
from the phone (facts: For the owner), and listing every interface is a
follow-up.

### Decision 4: static paths on the allowlisted port

The served set, all `GET`, all before authentication, matched exactly
in `serve_remote` (`src/app.rs:3017-3024`) ahead of the `/api/v1/`
prefix so the allowlist stays in one place:

| Path | Content-Type | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` | `web/index.html` |
| `/app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.css` |
| `/app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.js` |

Every other path, `/index.html` and `/app.js/` included, and every
other method on these three, stays 404 `not_found` as today. Each
static reply carries:

- `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
  style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none';
  form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src 'self'`
  covers the same-host `wss://` in CSP3 and WebKit since 2022
  (facts: Settled). No inline script, no inline style, no external
  resource: the HTML has one `<link>` and one `<script src>`.
- `Cache-Control: no-store`, so a new version is what the next open
  gets and nothing is cached across versions.
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

Pool and window: a page load is unauthenticated and sits in the
four-slot stranger pool (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `remote.rs:567`) until
its first authenticated reply. The count the page is designed to: three
load connections for the three files, kept alive; the first
authenticated request is a `fetch` of `/api/v1/waiting`, which moves its
connection to the paired pool and frees a slot; the WebSocket opens only
after that reply, as the fourth stranger at worst. Whether a browser
retries a dropped extra connection is unresolved (facts: Unresolved);
the poll fallback (page step 5) covers a socket that was dropped. The
three paths get
their own rate window, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 120` per listener (a reload
is three requests), beside `PAIR_PER_MINUTE` and `INFO_PER_MINUTE`
(`remote.rs:584-587`, `Limits::limited` at 631), answered 429 past it
without reaching the frame. §4.1's bounds list gains the line.

`RemoteReply` (`remote.rs:389-393`) gains an additive field
`headers: Vec<(String, String)>`, written after `Content-Length` by
`respond` (`remote.rs:530-554`), which takes the reply rather than
`(status, body)`; `Content-Type` is a header in that list, defaulting
to `application/json` when absent, so the 28 literals in `src/app.rs`
and the two in the adapter change only by `headers: Vec::new()`.
`Set-Cookie` travels the same way. `Served::Now`
(`app.rs:277-280`) is how the static replies go out; bodies are
`include_str!` constants in a new `src/web.rs` (`pub const INDEX_HTML`,
`APP_CSS`, `APP_JS`), the pattern of `include_bytes!` for the icon and
fonts (`src/main.rs:167`, `src/ui/theme.rs:203-211`). Nothing in

### What the page does (`web/app.js`)

In order, on load:

1. Read `location.hash`; if it names `code`, `key` and `id`, call
   `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` before any request. The
   fragment never reaches the host (facts: Settled); a copy in the
   browser's history is a spent single-use code once pairing succeeds
   or the window closes (facts: Unresolved on `replaceState` and
   history; `docs/remote-client.md:311` on single use), and the plan
   says so in the spec's new paragraph rather than promising more.
2. `GET /api/v1/info`. If the stored `server_id` matches and
   `spki_sha256` differs: show "This host's identity changed. Pair
   again." and send nothing else. If the URL's `key` differs from
   `/info`'s: show "This is not the host whose code was scanned." and
   do not post the code.
3. With a code and a matching key: `POST /api/v1/pair` with
   `{code, spki_sha256, device_name, transport: "cookie"}`;
   `device_name` from `navigator.userAgent` as "Safari on iPhone",
   "Chrome on Android", "Safari on Mac"; an iPad presents as a Mac
   (facts: Settled), so `Macintosh` with `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1`
   is "Safari on iPad". Store `server_id` and `spki_sha256`. A 403
   `wrong_code` or `pairing_closed` is shown by its message.
4. `GET /api/v1/waiting`, the first authenticated request. A 401 here
   with no pairing ever stored shows "Not paired. Open Remote devices on the Mac and scan the code."; a 401
   with a stored pairing shows "This device was revoked. Pair again."
   (the cookie is already cleared by the host). Then step 5, then
   `/projects` and `/projects/{id}/sessions` per project.
5. Open `wss://<host>/api/v1/events` after the `/waiting` reply of
   step 4 and before the `projects` and `sessions` snapshots (so one
   connection is already in the paired pool, Decision 4), buffer
   events, apply by revision (§4.4 "Subscribe first, then snapshot":
   the collections are the snapshot, `/waiting` is refetched if an
   event's revision passes its own),
   send `watch {kind, id}` for the open session's `conversation` or
   `screen` key. On open failure or close: poll `waiting`, `projects`
   and the open session's content every 5 s, refetching a collection
   whose `revision` moved, and retry the socket every 30 s. Header says
   "live" or "polling".
6. Render: sessions grouped by project, waiting first within and across
   groups, each with kind, the card word, the waiting reason; tapping
   one opens the view: `GET sessions/{id}/last-response` for a Claude
   Code session (`text`, as `client/Fixtures/last_response.json`),
   `GET sessions/{id}/screen` for anything else (`text`), refreshed on
   `changed {conversation|screen}` or on the poll. A reply box posts
   `POST sessions/{id}/send {op, text}` with a fresh UUID `op`, shown
   only when `/pair`'s or the stored `scope` is `control`; the device's
   scope and the host's `server_name` are in the header. Scope is not
   on `/info`, so a scope lowered in the dialog reaches the page as the
   403 its next `send` answers, which it shows as "This device is
   read-only now."

# Plan for #230: a web control surface on the remote port

Worktree `/Users/sbgragent/.dispatch/worktrees/f96f6569` at 0.4.1; every
line number is from this tree. One commit; the app runs at every step.
Facts are cited as `facts: Settled`, `facts: Unresolved` or `facts: For
the owner`.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **The session list carries no excerpt.** The issue's list shows "the
  one-line excerpt the card shows". No wire view carries one yet:
  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has `card`, `waiting`
  and `waiting_reason` and no excerpt field, and adding one is a wire
  crate change plus masking on the frame (`docs/remote-client.md:201`),
  outside this cut. The list shows kind, the card's word and the
  waiting reason; the session view shows the last response or the
  screen. The spec sentence at `docs/remote-client.md:207` is reworded
  in this commit to say the field is not yet on the wire; the field is
  a known gap in design.md.
- **The code rides in the URL's fragment, not its query.** The issue
  writes `/?code=…`. A fragment is never sent to the server (facts:
  Settled, RFC 3986 §3.5), so the code cannot reach a request log by
  any future change to `refuse`, which today logs path without query
  (`src/app.rs:3754-3766`). The page reads `location.hash` and clears
  it the same way the issue says; the camera-to-browser unknown is the
  same for both forms (facts: For the owner). The URL is
  `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
- **The browser's trust step is the certificate warning, and the page
  works without the WebSocket.** The issue offers click-through or a
  downloadable certificate. Downloading cannot work with the identity
  the spec fixed: iOS trusts no server certificate without a SAN, over
  825 days or without EKU (facts: Settled, Apple 103769), and lists a
  certificate for trust only when it is CA-shaped (facts: Settled, Apple
  DTS), so "download" means a CA plus a leaf, a different identity model
  from `docs/remote-client.md:307-308` (one self-signed certificate,
  SPKI pinned). That is a follow-up for the owner, not this plan. The
  click-through is the trust step, said in the dialog. Whether the
  bypass extends to `wss://` on iOS Safari is unresolved (facts:
  Unresolved, against it), so the page polls over `fetch` by default and
  the socket is the enhancement behind it.
- Everything else in the issue is as the tree bears it out.

## The record

No record changes. A browser is a `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:95-108`)
written by `Effect::SaveDevices` on `AppAction::Paired`
(`src/core/remote.rs:66-72`), its name from the page's user agent,
listed and revoked in the dialog as any device. No serialized type
changes, so no schema bump.

The page's state on the device: the token is in an `HttpOnly` cookie
the host sets and script never reads; the page keeps only `server_id`
and `spki_sha256` from the pairing in `localStorage`, to say "identity
changed" later (both are public, `/info` serves them to anyone).

## The signals

No new signal.

## The actions and effects

No new `AppAction` or `Effect`. The changes are in the adapter, the
frame's request routing, and one pure function in the core.

### Decision 1: browser trust (the click-through)

The warning the owner clicks through on the local network is the trust
step. What the `key` in the URL buys: a genuine page refuses to post the
code to a host whose `/info` key differs, which is the native client's
check; what it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not a
genuine page, so the owner's eyes on the warning, on their own network,
stand in for the SPKI pin. The paired-devices dialog says so in one
sentence (UI below). The host side is unchanged: no non-loopback bind
serves anything but `/info`, `/pair` and now the three page files before
pairing (§5, `docs/remote-client.md:306` amended). Chrome remembers the
bypass for a week per host (facts: Settled); Safari's persistence is
unknown (facts: Unresolved), so the dialog's sentence says the warning
may return and the page loses nothing when it does (the cookie and the
stored ids survive a reload).

### Decision 2: the token reaches the WebSocket as a cookie

The cookie is the safer store (script cannot read an `HttpOnly` cookie;
anything in `localStorage` or a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value is in
script), and the settled facts say it reaches both `fetch` and the
WebSocket on an IP origin with `Secure; SameSite=Strict` and no `Domain`
(facts: Settled, RFC 6265bis and HTML "obtain a site"). Whether a browser
stores a `Secure` cookie on a bypassed-certificate origin is unresolved
(facts: Unresolved): **that is the first thing the implementer tests on
a phone, before anything else is built**, with the host's `/pair`
answering a cookie and a `curl`-free check that `/api/v1/waiting` then
answers 200 from the page. If it fails, the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`
transport is a follow-up (end of plan), not a second transport built
now. The page shows "pair again" when its first authenticated call after
`/pair` is refused, so a dropped cookie is a visible state, never a
silent one.

Mechanics:

- `POST /api/v1/pair` takes an additive body field `"transport":
  "cookie"`. With it, the reply body omits `token` and carries
  `Set-Cookie: switchboard_token=<token>; Path=/api/v1/; Secure;
  HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`. Without it (the headset, the CLI,
  `tests/remote.rs::pair` at 406) the reply is as today, token in the
  body, no cookie. `remote_pair` (`src/app.rs:3606-3674`) is the only
  change on the frame; `Path=/api/v1/` keeps the cookie off the page
  files, which need none.
- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-517`) reads the `cookie`
  header, finds the `switchboard_token=` pair, and puts its value in a
  new `RemoteRequest::cookie: Option<String>` field. `authenticate`
  (`src/app.rs:3127-3157`) takes `bearer` first and `cookie` second:
  the native clients are unchanged, and a browser never sets the
  bearer. The WebSocket upgrade authenticates on the same request, so
  the socket needs nothing new; `respond_upgrade`
  (`remote.rs:519-527`) is unchanged.
- A 401 for an unknown cookie token (revoked, or every token after a key
  rotation) carries `Set-Cookie: switchboard_token=; Path=/api/v1/;
  Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, so the browser drops
  it. The refusal text stays "the token is not known; pair again":
  "revoked" and "never paired" remain one answer on the wire (facts:
  Settled), and the page tells them apart itself (UI below).
- `SameSite=Strict` is the cross-site guard: a page on another origin
  cannot make the browser attach the cookie to a `fetch` or a WebSocket
  handshake to the host. No `Origin` check is added.
- The spec's "never in a URL" rule stands (`docs/remote-client.md:312`);
  the sentence gains "or as the cookie `/pair` sets for a browser".

### Decision 3: one invite, the URL

The QR and "Copy invite" carry the URL. A new pure function in
`src/core/remote.rs`, `pairing_invite(identity: &Identity, address:
&str, code: &str) -> String`, builds it (IPv6 bracketed, code uppercase,
`key` the full hex `spki_sha256` so the page compares it with `/info`
by string equality), shared by the dialog, `tests/remote.rs` and
`src/core/tests.rs`. The URL is 153 bytes, QR version 9 at 53 modules,
smaller than today's JSON at version 10 (facts: Settled); `QR_SCALE`
(`src/ui/remote.rs:42`) stays 4, and rises only if the owner finds it
unreadable (facts: For the owner). The JSON form is no longer produced
by the host; the native text path keeps parsing it so an old copied
invite still works:

- `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114-116`)
  branches: text starting with `https://` has its authority taken as
  text, the substring between `https://` and the first `/`, straight
  into `addresses: [that]`, so the brackets the host wrote around an
  IPv6 literal survive; the fragment after `#` is split on `&` into
  `code`, `key`, `id`. Anything else is the JSON as today. `parse` uses
  nothing from `SwitchboardTransport`. `switchboard-remote pair
  '<url>'` (`main.swift:107-125`), the headset's paste field
  (`BrowserView.swift:883`) and `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` per line
  (`BrowserView.swift:104-108`) all pass through `parse` and need no
  other change; the three-argument CLI path (`main.swift:112-118`) is
  unchanged.

Without a network address (`remote::local_address()` is `None`,
`remote.rs:962-973`) there is no URL: the dialog shows the code and the
key with no QR and no Copy invite, and the sentence says to pair by the
CLI's three-argument form. The address is the default route's source
(facts: Settled); a VPN taking the default route makes it unreachable
from the phone (facts: For the owner), and listing every interface is a
follow-up.

### Decision 4: static paths on the allowlisted port

The served set, all `GET`, all before authentication, matched exactly
in `serve_remote` (`src/app.rs:3017-3024`) ahead of the `/api/v1/`
prefix so the allowlist stays in one place:

| Path | Content-Type | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` | `web/index.html` |
| `/app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.css` |
| `/app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.js` |

Every other path, `/index.html` and `/app.js/` included, and every
other method on these three, stays 404 `not_found` as today. Each
static reply carries:

- `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
  style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none';
  form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src 'self'`
  covers the same-host `wss://` in CSP3 and WebKit since 2022
  (facts: Settled). No inline script, no inline style, no external
  resource: the HTML has one `<link>` and one `<script src>`.
- `Cache-Control: no-store`, so a new version is what the next open
  gets and nothing is cached across versions.
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

Pool and window: a page load is unauthenticated and sits in the
four-slot stranger pool (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `remote.rs:567`) until
its first authenticated reply. The count the page is designed to: three
load connections for the three files, kept alive; the first
authenticated request is a `fetch` of `/api/v1/waiting`, which moves its
connection to the paired pool and frees a slot; the WebSocket opens only
after that reply, as the fourth stranger at worst. Whether a browser
retries a dropped extra connection is unresolved (facts: Unresolved);
the poll fallback (page step 5) covers a socket that was dropped. The
three paths get
their own rate window, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 120` per listener (a reload
is three requests), beside `PAIR_PER_MINUTE` and `INFO_PER_MINUTE`
(`remote.rs:584-587`, `Limits::limited` at 631), answered 429 past it
without reaching the frame. §4.1's bounds list gains the line.

`RemoteReply` (`remote.rs:389-393`) gains an additive field
`headers: Vec<(String, String)>`, written after `Content-Length` by
`respond` (`remote.rs:530-554`), which takes the reply rather than
`(status, body)`; `Content-Type` is a header in that list, defaulting
to `application/json` when absent, so the 28 literals in `src/app.rs`
and the two in the adapter change only by `headers: Vec::new()`.
`Set-Cookie` travels the same way. `Served::Now`
(`app.rs:277-280`) is how the static replies go out; bodies are
`include_str!` constants in a new `src/web.rs` (`pub const INDEX_HTML`,
`APP_CSS`, `APP_JS`), the pattern of `include_bytes!` for the icon and
fonts (`src/main.rs:167`, `src/ui/theme.rs:203-211`). Nothing in
`Cargo.toml` changes.

### What the page does (`web/app.js`)

In order, on load:

1. Read `location.hash`; if it names `code`, `key` and `id`, call
   `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` before any request. The
   fragment never reaches the host (facts: Settled); a copy in the
   browser's history is a spent single-use code once pairing succeeds
   or the window closes (facts: Unresolved on `replaceState` and
   history; `docs/remote-client.md:311` on single use), and the plan
   says so in the spec's new paragraph rather than promising more.
2. `GET /api/v1/info`. If the stored `server_id` matches and
   `spki_sha256` differs: show "This host's identity changed. Pair
   again." and send nothing else. If the URL's `key` differs from
   `/info`'s: show "This is not the host whose code was scanned." and
   do not post the code.
3. With a code and a matching key: `POST /api/v1/pair` with
   `{code, spki_sha256, device_name, transport: "cookie"}`;
   `device_name` from `navigator.userAgent` as "Safari on iPhone",
   "Chrome on Android", "Safari on Mac"; an iPad presents as a Mac
   (facts: Settled), so `Macintosh` with `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1`
   is "Safari on iPad". Store `server_id` and `spki_sha256`. A 403
   `wrong_code` or `pairing_closed` is shown by its message.
4. `GET /api/v1/waiting`, the first authenticated request. A 401 here
   with no pairing ever stored shows "Not paired. Open Remote devices on the Mac and scan the code."; a 401
   with a stored pairing shows "This device was revoked. Pair again."
   (the cookie is already cleared by the host). Then step 5, then
   `/projects` and `/projects/{id}/sessions` per project.
5. Open `wss://<host>/api/v1/events` after the `/waiting` reply of
   step 4 and before the `projects` and `sessions` snapshots (so one
   connection is already in the paired pool, Decision 4), buffer
   events, apply by revision (§4.4 "Subscribe first, then snapshot":
   the collections are the snapshot, `/waiting` is refetched if an
   event's revision passes its own),
   send `watch {kind, id}` for the open session's `conversation` or
   `screen` key. On open failure or close: poll `waiting`, `projects`
   and the open session's content every 5 s, refetching a collection
   whose `revision` moved, and retry the socket every 30 s. Header says
   "live" or "polling".
6. Render: sessions grouped by project, waiting first within and across
   groups, each with kind, the card word, the waiting reason; tapping
   one opens the view: `GET sessions/{id}/last-response` for a Claude
   Code session (`text`, as `client/Fixtures/last_response.json`),
   `GET sessions/{id}/screen` for anything else (`text`), refreshed on
   `changed {conversation|screen}` or on the poll. A reply box posts
   `POST sessions/{id}/send {op, text}` with a fresh UUID `op`, shown
   only when `/pair`'s or the stored `scope` is `control`; the device's
   scope and the host's `server_name` are in the header. Scope is not
   on `/info`, so a scope lowered in the dialog reaches the page as the
   403 its next `send` answers, which it shows as "This device is
   read-only now."

No framework, no build step: three files, plain DOM.

## The UI

`src/ui/remote.rs` `pairing` (141-228): the payload at 160-165 becomes
`core::remote::pairing_invite(..)`; the sentence becomes "Scan with a
phone's camera, or paste the invite into a client. The browser will
warn about the certificate: on your own network, accepting it is the
trust step, and it may ask again. Grants … scope. Open for five
minutes or three wrong codes." Without an address: no QR, no Copy
invite, "No network address: pair by `switchboard-remote pair
<host:port> <code> <key>`". `devices` (230-276) is unchanged: a browser
row reads "Safari on iPhone", read or control, paired and seen ago,
Revoke. No new script line: `pairing <code>` and `remote-devices`

### Decision 1: browser trust (the click-through)

The warning the owner clicks through on the local network is the trust
step. What the `key` in the URL buys: a genuine page refuses to post the
code to a host whose `/info` key differs, which is the native client's
check; what it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not a
genuine page, so the owner's eyes on the warning, on their own network,
stand in for the SPKI pin. The paired-devices dialog says so in one
sentence (UI below). The host side is unchanged: no non-loopback bind

pairing (§5, `docs/remote-client.md:306` amended). Chrome remembers the
bypass for a week per host (facts: Settled); Safari's persistence is
unknown (facts: Unresolved), so the dialog's sentence says the warning
may return and the page loses nothing when it does (the cookie and the
stored ids survive a reload).

### Decision 2: the token reaches the WebSocket as a cookie

The cookie is the safer store (script cannot read an `HttpOnly` cookie;
anything in `localStorage` or a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value is in
script), and the settled facts say it reaches both `fetch` and the

answers 200 from the page. If it fails, the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`
transport is a follow-up (end of plan), not a second transport built

silent one.

2. `GET /api/v1/info`. If the stored `server_id` matches and
   `spki_sha256` differs: show "This host's identity changed. Pair
   again." and send nothing else. If the URL's `key` differs from
   `/info`'s: show "This is not the host whose code was scanned." and
   do not post the code.
3. With a code and a matching key: `POST /api/v1/pair` with

   the collections are the snapshot, `/waiting` is refetched if an
   event's revision passes its own),

# Plan for #230: a web control surface on the remote port

Worktree `/Users/sbgragent/.dispatch/worktrees/f96f6569` at 0.4.1; every
line number is from this tree. One commit; the app runs at every step.
Facts are cited as `facts: Settled`, `facts: Unresolved` or `facts: For
the owner`.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **The session list carries no excerpt.** The issue's list shows "the
  one-line excerpt the card shows". No wire view carries one yet:
  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has `card`, `waiting`
  and `waiting_reason` and no excerpt field, and adding one is a wire
  crate change plus masking on the frame (`docs/remote-client.md:201`),
  outside this cut. The list shows kind, the card's word and the
  waiting reason; the session view shows the last response or the
  screen. The spec sentence at `docs/remote-client.md:207` is reworded
  in this commit to say the field is not yet on the wire; the field is
  a known gap in design.md.
- **The code rides in the URL's fragment, not its query.** The issue
  writes `/?code=…`. A fragment is never sent to the server (facts:
  Settled, RFC 3986 §3.5), so the code cannot reach a request log by
  any future change to `refuse`, which today logs path without query
  (`src/app.rs:3754-3766`). The page reads `location.hash` and clears
  it the same way the issue says; the camera-to-browser unknown is the
  same for both forms (facts: For the owner). The URL is
  `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
- **The browser's trust step is the certificate warning, and the page
  works without the WebSocket.** The issue offers click-through or a
  downloadable certificate. Downloading cannot work with the identity
  the spec fixed: iOS trusts no server certificate without a SAN, over
  825 days or without EKU (facts: Settled, Apple 103769), and lists a
  certificate for trust only when it is CA-shaped (facts: Settled, Apple
  DTS), so "download" means a CA plus a leaf, a different identity model
  from `docs/remote-client.md:307-308` (one self-signed certificate,
  SPKI pinned). That is a follow-up for the owner, not this plan. The
  click-through is the trust step, said in the dialog. Whether the
  bypass extends to `wss://` on iOS Safari is unresolved (facts:
  Unresolved, against it), so the page polls over `fetch` by default and
  the socket is the enhancement behind it.
- Everything else in the issue is as the tree bears it out.

## The record

No record changes. A browser is a `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:95-108`)
written by `Effect::SaveDevices` on `AppAction::Paired`
(`src/core/remote.rs:66-72`), its name from the page's user agent,
listed and revoked in the dialog as any device. No serialized type
changes, so no schema bump.

The page's state on the device: the token is in an `HttpOnly` cookie
the host sets and script never reads; the page keeps only `server_id`
and `spki_sha256` from the pairing in `localStorage`, to say "identity
changed" later (both are public, `/info` serves them to anyone).

## The signals

No new signal.

## The actions and effects

No new `AppAction` or `Effect`. The changes are in the adapter, the
frame's request routing, and one pure function in the core.

### Decision 1: browser trust (the click-through)

The warning the owner clicks through on the local network is the trust
step. What the `key` in the URL buys: a genuine page refuses to post the
code to a host whose `/info` key differs, which is the native client's
check; what it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not a
genuine page, so the owner's eyes on the warning, on their own network,
stand in for the SPKI pin. The paired-devices dialog says so in one
sentence (UI below). The host side is unchanged: no non-loopback bind
serves anything but `/info`, `/pair` and now the three page files before
pairing (§5, `docs/remote-client.md:306` amended). Chrome remembers the
bypass for a week per host (facts: Settled); Safari's persistence is
unknown (facts: Unresolved), so the dialog's sentence says the warning
may return and the page loses nothing when it does (the cookie and the
stored ids survive a reload).

### Decision 2: the token reaches the WebSocket as a cookie

The cookie is the safer store (script cannot read an `HttpOnly` cookie;
anything in `localStorage` or a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value is in
script), and the settled facts say it reaches both `fetch` and the
WebSocket on an IP origin with `Secure; SameSite=Strict` and no `Domain`
(facts: Settled, RFC 6265bis and HTML "obtain a site"). Whether a browser
stores a `Secure` cookie on a bypassed-certificate origin is unresolved
(facts: Unresolved): **that is the first thing the implementer tests on
a phone, before anything else is built**, with the host's `/pair`
answering a cookie and a `curl`-free check that `/api/v1/waiting` then
answers 200 from the page. If it fails, the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`
transport is a follow-up (end of plan), not a second transport built
now. The page shows "pair again" when its first authenticated call after
`/pair` is refused, so a dropped cookie is a visible state, never a
silent one.

Mechanics:

- The cookie is named for the host: `switchboard_token_<server_id>`,
  the `server_id` UUID the pair reply already carries
  (`src/app.rs:3606-3674`, `"server_id": identity.server_id`; hex and
  hyphens, a valid cookie-name token). Cookies are scoped by host and
  path, not port, so two instances on one Mac (the README's dev-aid
  setup) share a jar: a fixed name would have the second pairing
  overwrite the first's token. The server id is kept across a key
  rotation (`make_identity` is called with `Some(identity.server_id)`,
  `src/app.rs:2811`), so the name is stable for a host's life. One pure
  function, `core::remote::token_cookie_name(&Identity) -> String`,
  builds the name for the `Set-Cookie` and for the lookup.
- `POST /api/v1/pair` takes an additive body field `"transport":
  "cookie"`. With it, the reply body omits `token` and carries
  `Set-Cookie: switchboard_token_<server_id>=<token>; Path=/api/v1/;
  Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`. Without it (the headset, the CLI,
  `tests/remote.rs::pair` at 406) the reply is as today, token in the
  body, no cookie. `remote_pair` (`src/app.rs:3606-3674`) is the only
  change on the frame; `Path=/api/v1/` keeps the cookie off the page
  files, which need none.
- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-517`) does not know the
  host's id, and the browser may send several hosts' cookies in one
  header, so it reads the `cookie` header and keeps every pair whose
  name starts `switchboard_token_` in a new
  `RemoteRequest::cookies: Vec<(String, String)>` field (name, value).
  `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127-3157`) takes `bearer` first and,
  failing that, the cookie named `token_cookie_name(identity)`; a
  cookie for another host is ignored, not an error. The native clients
  are unchanged, and a browser never sets the bearer. The WebSocket
  upgrade authenticates on the same request, so the socket needs
  nothing new; `respond_upgrade` (`remote.rs:519-527`) is unchanged.
- A 401 for an unknown token from this host's own cookie (revoked, or
  every token after a key rotation) carries `Set-Cookie:
  switchboard_token_<server_id>=; Path=/api/v1/; Max-Age=0; Secure;
  HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, so the browser drops it; a 401 with no
  cookie of this host's name clears nothing, and never touches another
  host's cookie. The refusal text stays "the token is not known; pair again":
  "revoked" and "never paired" remain one answer on the wire (facts:
  Settled), and the page tells them apart itself (UI below).
- Two instances on one IP differ by port only; the per-host name keeps
  their tokens apart, and each instance's lookup ignores the other's
  cookie.
- `SameSite=Strict` is the cross-site guard: a page on another origin
  cannot make the browser attach the cookie to a `fetch` or a WebSocket
  handshake to the host. No `Origin` check is added.
- The spec's "never in a URL" rule stands (`docs/remote-client.md:312`);
  the sentence gains "or as the cookie `/pair` sets for a browser".

### Decision 3: one invite, the URL

The QR and "Copy invite" carry the URL. A new pure function in
`src/core/remote.rs`, `pairing_invite(identity: &Identity, address:
&str, code: &str) -> String`, builds it (IPv6 bracketed, code uppercase,
`key` the full hex `spki_sha256` so the page compares it with `/info`
by string equality), shared by the dialog, `tests/remote.rs` and
`src/core/tests.rs`. The URL is 153 bytes, QR version 9 at 53 modules,
smaller than today's JSON at version 10 (facts: Settled); `QR_SCALE`
(`src/ui/remote.rs:42`) stays 4, and rises only if the owner finds it
unreadable (facts: For the owner). The JSON form is no longer produced
by the host; the native text path keeps parsing it so an old copied
invite still works:

- `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114-116`)

  text, the substring between `https://` and the first `/`, straight

  IPv6 literal survive; the fragment after `#` is split on `&` into
  `code`, `key`, `id`. Anything else is the JSON as today. `parse` uses
  nothing from `SwitchboardTransport`. `switchboard-remote pair
  '<url>'` (`main.swift:107-125`), the headset's paste field
  (`BrowserView.swift:883`) and `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` per line
  (`BrowserView.swift:104-108`) all pass through `parse` and need no
  other change; the three-argument CLI path (`main.swift:112-118`) is

Without a network address (`remote::local_address()` is `None`,
`remote.rs:962-973`) there is no URL: the dialog shows the code and the
key with no QR and no Copy invite, and the sentence says to pair by the
CLI's three-argument form. The address is the default route's source
(facts: Settled); a VPN taking the default route makes it unreachable
from the phone (facts: For the owner), and listing every interface is a
follow-up.

### Decision 4: static paths on the allowlisted port

The served set, all `GET`, all before authentication, matched exactly

| Path | Content-Type | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` | `web/index.html` |
| `/app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.css` |
| `/app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.js` |

Every other path, `/index.html` and `/app.js/` included, and every
other method on these three, stays 404 `not_found` as today. Each
static reply carries:

- `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
  style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none';
  form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src 'self'`
  covers the same-host `wss://` in CSP3 and WebKit since 2022
  (facts: Settled). No inline script, no inline style, no external
  resource: the HTML has one `<link>` and one `<script src>`.
- `Cache-Control: no-store`, so a new version is what the next open
  gets and nothing is cached across versions.
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

four-slot stranger pool (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `remote.rs:567`) until

load connections for the three files, kept alive; the first
authenticated request is a `fetch` of `/api/v1/waiting`, which moves its

the poll fallback (page step 5) covers a socket that was dropped. The
three paths get

and the two in the adapter change only by `headers: Vec::new()`.
`Set-Cookie` travels the same way. `Served::Now`
(`app.rs:277-280`) is how the static replies go out; bodies are

1. Read `location.hash`; if it names `code`, `key` and `id`, call

# Plan for #230: a web control surface on the remote port

Worktree `/Users/sbgragent/.dispatch/worktrees/f96f6569` at 0.4.1; every
line number is from this tree. One commit; the app runs at every step.
Facts are cited as `facts: Settled`, `facts: Unresolved` or `facts: For
the owner`.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **The session list carries no excerpt.** The issue's list shows "the
  one-line excerpt the card shows". No wire view carries one yet:
  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has `card`, `waiting`
  and `waiting_reason` and no excerpt field, and adding one is a wire
  crate change plus masking on the frame (`docs/remote-client.md:201`),
  outside this cut. The list shows kind, the card's word and the
  waiting reason; the session view shows the last response or the
  screen. The spec sentence at `docs/remote-client.md:207` is reworded
  in this commit to say the field is not yet on the wire; the field is
  a known gap in design.md.
- **The code rides in the URL's fragment, not its query.** The issue
  writes `/?code=…`. A fragment is never sent to the server (facts:
  Settled, RFC 3986 §3.5), so the code cannot reach a request log by
  any future change to `refuse`, which today logs path without query
  (`src/app.rs:3754-3766`). The page reads `location.hash` and clears
  it the same way the issue says; the camera-to-browser unknown is the
  same for both forms (facts: For the owner). The URL is
  `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
- **The browser's trust step is the certificate warning, and the page
  works without the WebSocket.** The issue offers click-through or a
  downloadable certificate. Downloading cannot work with the identity
  the spec fixed: iOS trusts no server certificate without a SAN, over
  825 days or without EKU (facts: Settled, Apple 103769), and lists a
  certificate for trust only when it is CA-shaped (facts: Settled, Apple
  DTS), so "download" means a CA plus a leaf, a different identity model
  from `docs/remote-client.md:307-308` (one self-signed certificate,
  SPKI pinned). That is a follow-up for the owner, not this plan. The
  click-through is the trust step, said in the dialog. Whether the
  bypass extends to `wss://` on iOS Safari is unresolved (facts:
  Unresolved, against it), so the page polls over `fetch` by default and
  the socket is the enhancement behind it.
- Everything else in the issue is as the tree bears it out.

## The record

No record changes. A browser is a `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:95-108`)
written by `Effect::SaveDevices` on `AppAction::Paired`
(`src/core/remote.rs:66-72`), its name from the page's user agent,
listed and revoked in the dialog as any device. No serialized type
changes, so no schema bump.

The page's state on the device: the token is in an `HttpOnly` cookie
the host sets and script never reads; the page keeps only `server_id`
and `spki_sha256` from the pairing in `localStorage`, to say "identity
changed" later (both are public, `/info` serves them to anyone).

## The signals

No new signal.

## The actions and effects

No new `AppAction` or `Effect`. The changes are in the adapter, the
frame's request routing, and one pure function in the core.

### Decision 1: browser trust (the click-through)

The warning the owner clicks through on the local network is the trust
step. What the `key` in the URL buys: a genuine page refuses to post the
code to a host whose `/info` key differs, which is the native client's
check; what it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not a
genuine page, so the owner's eyes on the warning, on their own network,
stand in for the SPKI pin. The paired-devices dialog says so in one
sentence (UI below). The host side is unchanged: no non-loopback bind
serves anything but `/info`, `/pair` and now the three page files before
pairing (§5, `docs/remote-client.md:306` amended). Chrome remembers the
bypass for a week per host (facts: Settled); Safari's persistence is
unknown (facts: Unresolved), so the dialog's sentence says the warning
may return and the page loses nothing when it does (the cookie and the
stored ids survive a reload).

### Decision 2: the token reaches the WebSocket as a cookie

The cookie is the safer store (script cannot read an `HttpOnly` cookie;
anything in `localStorage` or a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value is in
script), and the settled facts say it reaches both `fetch` and the
WebSocket on an IP origin with `Secure; SameSite=Strict` and no `Domain`
(facts: Settled, RFC 6265bis and HTML "obtain a site"). Whether a browser
stores a `Secure` cookie on a bypassed-certificate origin is unresolved
(facts: Unresolved): **that is the first thing the implementer tests on
a phone, before anything else is built**, with the host's `/pair`
answering a cookie and a `curl`-free check that `/api/v1/waiting` then
answers 200 from the page. If it fails, the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`
transport is a follow-up (end of plan), not a second transport built
now. The page shows "pair again" when its first authenticated call after
`/pair` is refused, so a dropped cookie is a visible state, never a
silent one.

Mechanics:

- The cookie is named for the host: `switchboard_token_<server_id>`,
  the `server_id` UUID the pair reply already carries
  (`src/app.rs:3606-3674`, `"server_id": identity.server_id`; hex and
  hyphens, a valid cookie-name token). Cookies are scoped by host and
  path, not port, so two instances on one Mac (the README's dev-aid
  setup) share a jar: a fixed name would have the second pairing
  overwrite the first's token. The server id is kept across a key
  rotation (`make_identity` is called with `Some(identity.server_id)`,
  `src/app.rs:2811`), so the name is stable for a host's life. One pure
  function, `core::remote::token_cookie_name(&Identity) -> String`,
  builds the name for the `Set-Cookie` and for the lookup.
- `POST /api/v1/pair` takes an additive body field `"transport":
  "cookie"`. With it, the reply body omits `token` and carries
  `Set-Cookie: switchboard_token_<server_id>=<token>; Path=/api/v1/;
  Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`. Without it (the headset, the CLI,
  `tests/remote.rs::pair` at 406) the reply is as today, token in the
  body, no cookie. `remote_pair` (`src/app.rs:3606-3674`) is the only
  change on the frame; `Path=/api/v1/` keeps the cookie off the page
  files, which need none.
- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-517`) does not know the
  host's id, and the browser may send several hosts' cookies in one
  header, so it reads the `cookie` header and keeps every pair whose
  name starts `switchboard_token_` in a new
  `RemoteRequest::cookies: Vec<(String, String)>` field (name, value).
  `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127-3157`) takes `bearer` first and,
  failing that, the cookie named `token_cookie_name(identity)`; a
  cookie for another host is ignored, not an error. The native clients
  are unchanged, and a browser never sets the bearer. The WebSocket
  upgrade authenticates on the same request, so the socket needs
  nothing new; `respond_upgrade` (`remote.rs:519-527`) is unchanged.
- A 401 for an unknown token from this host's own cookie (revoked, or
  every token after a key rotation) carries `Set-Cookie:
  switchboard_token_<server_id>=; Path=/api/v1/; Max-Age=0; Secure;
  HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, so the browser drops it; a 401 with no
  cookie of this host's name clears nothing, and never touches another
  host's cookie. The refusal text stays "the token is not known; pair again":
  "revoked" and "never paired" remain one answer on the wire (facts:
  Settled), and the page tells them apart itself (UI below).
- Two instances on one IP differ by port only; the per-host name keeps
  their tokens apart, and each instance's lookup ignores the other's
  cookie.
- `SameSite=Strict` is the cross-site guard: a page on another origin
  cannot make the browser attach the cookie to a `fetch` or a WebSocket
  handshake to the host. No `Origin` check is added.
- The spec's "never in a URL" rule stands (`docs/remote-client.md:312`);
  the sentence gains "or as the cookie `/pair` sets for a browser".

### Decision 3: one invite, the URL

The QR and "Copy invite" carry the URL. A new pure function in
`src/core/remote.rs`, `pairing_invite(identity: &Identity, address:
&str, code: &str) -> String`, builds it (IPv6 bracketed, code uppercase,
`key` the full hex `spki_sha256` so the page compares it with `/info`
by string equality), shared by the dialog, `tests/remote.rs` and
`src/core/tests.rs`. The URL is 153 bytes, QR version 9 at 53 modules,
smaller than today's JSON at version 10 (facts: Settled); `QR_SCALE`
(`src/ui/remote.rs:42`) stays 4, and rises only if the owner finds it
unreadable (facts: For the owner). The JSON form is no longer produced
by the host; the native text path keeps parsing it so an old copied
invite still works:

- `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114-116`)
  branches: text starting with `https://` has its authority taken as
  text, the substring between `https://` and the first `/`, straight
  into `addresses: [that]`, so the brackets the host wrote around an
  IPv6 literal survive; the fragment after `#` is split on `&` into
  `code`, `key`, `id`. Anything else is the JSON as today. `parse` uses
  nothing from `SwitchboardTransport`. `switchboard-remote pair
  '<url>'` (`main.swift:107-125`), the headset's paste field
  (`BrowserView.swift:883`) and `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` per line
  (`BrowserView.swift:104-108`) all pass through `parse` and need no
  other change; the three-argument CLI path (`main.swift:112-118`) is
  unchanged.

Without a network address (`remote::local_address()` is `None`,
`remote.rs:962-973`) there is no URL: the dialog shows the code and the
key with no QR and no Copy invite, and the sentence says to pair by the
CLI's three-argument form. The address is the default route's source
(facts: Settled); a VPN taking the default route makes it unreachable
from the phone (facts: For the owner), and listing every interface is a
follow-up.

### Decision 4: static paths on the allowlisted port

The served set, all `GET`, all before authentication, matched exactly
in `serve_remote` (`src/app.rs:3017-3024`) ahead of the `/api/v1/`
prefix so the allowlist stays in one place:

| Path | Content-Type | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` | `web/index.html` |
| `/app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.css` |
| `/app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.js` |

Every other path, `/index.html` and `/app.js/` included, and every
other method on these three, stays 404 `not_found` as today. Each
static reply carries:

- `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
  style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none';
  form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src 'self'`
  covers the same-host `wss://` in CSP3 and WebKit since 2022
  (facts: Settled). No inline script, no inline style, no external
  resource: the HTML has one `<link>` and one `<script src>`.
- `Cache-Control: no-store`, so a new version is what the next open
  gets and nothing is cached across versions.
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

Pool and window: a page load is unauthenticated and sits in the
four-slot stranger pool (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `remote.rs:567`) until
its first authenticated reply. The count the page is designed to: three
load connections for the three files, kept alive; the first
authenticated request is a `fetch` of `/api/v1/waiting`, which moves its
connection to the paired pool and frees a slot; the WebSocket opens only
after that reply, as the fourth stranger at worst. Whether a browser
retries a dropped extra connection is unresolved (facts: Unresolved);
the poll fallback (page step 5) covers a socket that was dropped. The
three paths get
their own rate window, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 120` per listener (a reload
is three requests), beside `PAIR_PER_MINUTE` and `INFO_PER_MINUTE`
(`remote.rs:584-587`, `Limits::limited` at 631), answered 429 past it
without reaching the frame. §4.1's bounds list gains the line.

`RemoteReply` (`remote.rs:389-393`) gains an additive field
`headers: Vec<(String, String)>`, written after `Content-Length` by
`respond` (`remote.rs:530-554`), which takes the reply rather than
`(status, body)`; `Content-Type` is a header in that list, defaulting
to `application/json` when absent, so the 28 literals in `src/app.rs`
and the two in the adapter change only by `headers: Vec::new()`.

the owner`.

  one-line excerpt the card shows". No wire view carries one yet:
  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has `card`, `waiting`
  and `waiting_reason` and no excerpt field, and adding one is a wire
  crate change plus masking on the frame (`docs/remote-client.md:201`),

  waiting reason; the session view shows the last response or the
  screen. The spec sentence at `docs/remote-client.md:207` is reworded
  in this commit to say the field is not yet on the wire; the field is
  a known gap in design.md.

  writes `/?code=…`. A fragment is never sent to the server (facts:
  Settled, RFC 3986 §3.5), so the code cannot reach a request log by
  any future change to `refuse`, which today logs path without query

  certificate for trust only when it is CA-shaped (facts: Settled, Apple

  from `docs/remote-client.md:307-308` (one self-signed certificate,
  SPKI pinned). That is a follow-up for the owner, not this plan. The
  click-through is the trust step, said in the dialog. Whether the
  bypass extends to `wss://` on iOS Safari is unresolved (facts:
  Unresolved, against it), so the page polls over `fetch` by default and
  the socket is the enhancement behind it.

listed and revoked in the dialog as any device. No serialized type
changes, so no schema bump.

No new signal.

## The actions and effects

### Decision 1: browser trust (the click-through)

The warning the owner clicks through on the local network is the trust
step. What the `key` in the URL buys: a genuine page refuses to post the
code to a host whose `/info` key differs, which is the native client's
check; what it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not a
genuine page, so the owner's eyes on the warning, on their own network,
